Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Ms. Divya Jain, Advocate for the 
appellant.
Mr. Rakesh Negi, Brief Holder for the 
State.
The instant appeal has been preferred 
against the judgment and order dated 
24.01.2026, passed in Special Sessions Trial 
No.170 of 2024, State v. Parvez, by the court 
of Special Judge (POCSO)/Additional District 
Judge, Dehradun. It is delayed. Delay 
Condonation Application, IA No.02 of 2026, 
has been filed.
On the last occasion, the Court had 
directed for issuance of notice. In fact, 
issuance of notice is not required because 
respondent is State, which is represented 
before the Court. 
Heard on the delay condonation 
application.
The delay condonation application is 
not objected to by learned State Counsel. 
Having considered, we are of the view 
that there are good grounds for condonation 
of delay. Accordingly, the Delay Condonation 
Application deserves to be allowed.
The delay condonation application is 
allowed. 
The delay in preferring the appeal is 
condoned.  Heard on admission. 
Admit. 
Lower court record has already been 
received.
Let paper book be prepared and 
provided to learned counsel for the parties, as 
per rule.
List this matter on 05.08.2026, under 
the caption of Final Hearing. 
(Siddhartha Sah J.) (Ravindra Maithani J.) 
 29.06.2026

3. In fact, the issue in the instant matter is 
appointment of a teaching faculty in the 
University and the issue raised is that the marks 
were not awarded as per the prescribed procedure 
for research papers, conferences and seminars 
etc. 
4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the 
petitioner seeks time to file a supplementary  affidavit categorically bringing on record as to 
what marks the petitioner was entitled to and 
how much marks were given to him under 
different heads. He would also like to place on 
record as to what is the error or mistake made by
